title: Mexican Sunflower (Icyicamahirwe) around Bush Bean crop land

Header: Mexican Sunflower (Icyicamahirwe) around Bush Bean crop land

Prevention: Tithonia is frequently kept as controlled fence and source of forage to feed livestock
Use clean and certified seed to avoid accidental introduction
Leave at least 1m pathway between the crop field and
Tithonia hedge to avoid its invasion into the crop field
Monitoring: Soybean, Irish potato, groundnuts, peas and biodiversity
Annual or perennial herbaceous broadleaved shrub, woody at the base [2–3 (–5) m high].
Leaves greyish- green, flowers bright yellow, daisy or sunflower-like (up to 10 cm across), carried on long and swollen stalks (7–30 cm long).
Check for flowering and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank for
Tithonia planted as a hedge around the field crop
Tithonia plants in the crop field and take control action before flowering and seed set
Direct Control: During the rainy season, regularly cut
Either chop plants into pieces and heap them within the hedge to dry and decompose or feed to livestock
Tithonia plants emerging in the crop field.
Allow them to dry and decompose or feed them to livestock
Avoid leaving plant cuttings in the crop fields because
Restrictions: Rwanda herbicide application is not recommended as errant domestic animals usually feed on the weed.
